subject: computer-science
title: Logic Gates: Combining Gates
welcome_lead: Wire gates together to make decisions like a tiny computer.
meta_desc: KS3 logic gates: chaining AND/OR/NOT for two-step logic.
final_note: Real computers are AND/OR/NOT — just billions of them.

concepts.def: Gates connected together to produce output.
NOT after AND — only false when both true.
NOT after OR — only true when both false.
True when inputs differ — exclusive or.
Single 0 or 1 used as input or output.

walkthroughs.body_html: Wire the output of one gate into the input of another. AND followed by NOT gives NAND. OR followed by NOT gives NOR.
XOR is true when inputs are different — useful for testing equality and building adders.
Lots of gates wired together build adders, memory and finally a CPU. Each piece is simple; the whole is amazing.

mcqs.q: Which gate is true when inputs differ?

numericals.q: How many inputs does a basic NAND gate have?
